method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.reason: Signals a market-wide risk-off impulse driven by renewed AI fears; the piece highlights a shift in investor positioning (safe-haven rotation into Swiss stocks) which is symptomatic of broader negative sentiment for risk assets and AI-led leadership. Equities.title: Stocks fall, but tech shares steady after selloff; oil hits highest in nearly six months
Equities.reason: Broad market selloff with tech mixed captures immediate market reaction and negative risk sentiment. Relevant as a near-term market-moving datapoint reinforcing a risk-off regime and pressure on cyclical/leverage-sensitive names.

Equities.title: The Earnings Boom Is Heavily Reliant on Just a Handful of Stocks
Equities.reason: Reinforces the concentration narrative (earnings/market breadth driven by a few mega-cap names), a structural vulnerability that amplifies downside during rotations out of leadership. High relevance for market regime and portfolio construction implications.

Equities.title: Turmoil hits AI buildout as neoclouds face pressure, credit risks mount and Solidigm pulls IPO
Equities.summary: Stock slumps, pulled IPOs and rising spreads on credit default swaps this week sets stage for hyperscaler earnings.
Equities.reason: Combines sector-specific stress (AI/neoclouds) with rising credit risk and IPO withdrawals — a multi-channel negative that can materially affect tech capex, earnings, and investor appetite for high-growth names. Rated highly relevant because it ties equity performance to credit and capital-markets p

Equities.title: Nvidia's role as AI financier faces first big test as neoclouds take market hit
Equities.summary: As Nvidia has gone from chipmaker to industry financier, some investors see the company taking on outsized risk tied to the AI buildout.
Equities.reason: Highlights concentration and counterparty risk centered on a single market leader; negative for market sentiment given Nvidia's central role in the AI trade. Relevant as it affects investor positioning in large-cap tech and financing-linked exposures.

Equities.title: AI fever ignites a boom in thematic ETFs as fund managers hunt for their next big hit
Equities.reason: Documents persistent retail/institutional flows into AI-themed ETFs — a pro-risk/sector-concentration force that supports AI leadership despite pullbacks. Lower relevance than macro risk stories because it's a flow/fund-structure datapoint rather than immediate market shock.

Equities.title: Breaking: US S&P Global Composite PMI eases in October, Manufacturing at 53-month high
Equities.summary: Business activity in the United States (US) private sector showed continued expansion in October, according to preliminary data released by S&P Global on Friday.
Equities.reason: Macro PMI still signaling expansion supports cyclical earnings and provides a countervailing positive to short-term risk-off moves. Relevant as a macro backdrop input for equity positioning and rate/earnings outlooks.

Equities.title: Growth, Value Stocks Set for Reshuffle as S&P Adopts New Rules
Equities.reason: Index rule changes imply material rebalancing flows between growth and value categories; structurally important for sector and factor positioning. Moderate relevance because it can drive mechanically large reallocations even where fundamentals are unchanged.

Equities.title: ‘Total Meltdown’ in Riskiest Debt Unnerves Market: Credit Weekly
Equities.reason: Credit-market stress in the riskiest debt segments increases downside risk for equities by threatening funding/liquidity and investor risk appetite. Treated as a cross-market negative with above-average relevance for equity risk premia.

Equities.title: Barclays ‘House of Fixed Income’ Pins Future Growth on Equities
Equities.reason: Institutional positioning note: fixed-income business expecting growth from equities implies potential long-term allocation flows into equity markets. Lower relevance for near-term market moves but meaningful as a structural demand signal.

Rates.title: Japanese Yen pares gains as bond yields fall despite stronger inflation
Rates.summary: USD/JPY reverses earlier losses on Friday after slipping to a five-week low of 156.08 during Asian trading hours.
Rates.reason: Headline links FX move to falling bond yields — signals a modest bond rally (yields down), positive for bonds. Relevance moderate since the piece is FX-focused but explicitly cites bond yields.

Rates.title: Federal Reserve: October hold raises December hike odds - TD Securities
Rates.summary: TD Securities strategists expect the Federal Reserve (Fed) to keep the Fed Funds rate at 4.00% at the October FOMC meeting, despite strong inflation and solid labor data.
Rates.reason: Fed hold but stronger data lifts odds of a December hike — market-implied tightening increases term premia and Treasury yields (negative for bonds). High relevance given Fed policy implications for global rates.

Rates.title: Bank of Canada: Gradual return to neutral – TD Securities
Rates.summary: TD Securities’ macro team, led by Andrew Kelvin and Robert Both, does not share market conviction for an October Bank of Canada rate hike. They expect the BoC to hold at 2.25% now, then deliver 25bp increases in December and January, taking policy to the midpo
Rates.reason: Expectations of additional BoC hikes (return to neutral) imply higher Canadian yields and tighter domestic rates — negative for fixed income. Relevance elevated due to near-term hike timing.

Rates.title: Bank of Canada: Preemptive tightening focus – RBC
Rates.summary: Royal Bank of Canada economists Frances Donald and Nathan Janzen highlight the possibility of a 25 basis point Bank of Canada rate hike on Wednesday, while acknowledging that December or January remains an alternative.
Rates.reason: RBC highlights a near-term BoC hike risk — reinforces tightening narrative and upward pressure on yields, but is a regional/near-term call so slightly lower relevance.

Rates.title: South Korean Won: Hawkish BoK supports consolidation – Commerzbank
Rates.summary: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay and Dr. Henry Hao highlight that the Bank of Korea (BoK) kept its policy rate at 3.00% after two prior hikes, but delivered a clearly hawkish message. Strong semiconductor exports underpin higher growth expectations and rising inflati
Rates.reason: Hawkish BoK messaging supports expectations of higher local rates and upward pressure on Korean sovereign yields — negative for bonds, moderate relevance (regional central-bank signal).

Rates.title: Turkish Lira: CBRT maintains cautious easing stance - Commerzbank
Rates.summary: Tatha Ghose at Commerzbank reports that Turkey’s Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (CBRT) cut its one-week repo rate by 100bp to 36.0%, alongside similar moves in overnight rates.
Rates.reason: Large CBRT cut is an easing shock for domestic policy rates, likely to lower short-term yields locally (positive for bond prices in Turkey). Relevance limited to Turkish/EM rates.

Rates.title: What next for France as riots rattle markets? Three questions facing investors ahead of more protests
Rates.summary: French unrest pushed bond yields to a 24-year high as investors weigh budget, growth and sectors risks ahead of more protests.
Rates.reason: Political unrest has driven French yields sharply higher (24-year high) — a material widening/sovereign-risk event that is negative for European fixed income and raises risk premia.

Rates.title: Moody's holds steady on France's credit rating as country grapples with turmoil and higher yields
Rates.summary: Moody's left its credit rating on France at Aa3, giving the country some relief in a week of unrest.
Rates.reason: Rating agency decision to hold France's rating provides modest relief to sovereign spreads — small positive for bond markets but lower relevance versus the unrest-driven yield move.

FX.title: European Central Bank: One more hike then extended plateau – Commerzbank
FX.summary: Commerzbank economists expect the European Central Bank (ECB) to leave its deposit rate at 2.50% in October, then raise it to 2.75% in December in response to persistent Eurozone inflation.
FX.reason: ECB rate-hike expectation supports euro vs USD (EURUSD positive). The forecast is a policy-driven/central-bank signal with market relevance across EUR flows, but the 'one more hike then plateau' limits upside, so medium positive direction and moderate relevance.

FX.title: Canadian Dollar extends winning streak as Fed-BoC policy divergence comes into focus
FX.summary: USD/CAD slips below 1.4000 to its lowest level in a month on Friday, extending its losing streak to seven consecutive days as traders expect the Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Bank of Canada (BoC) to take different paths at next week’s meetings.
FX.reason: Clear CAD strength vs USD driven by expected policy divergence (BoC vs Fed). High relevance because it reflects sustained multi-day flow and near-term central-bank event risk that materially affects USD/CAD.

FX.title: US Dollar: Resilient into FOMC with election risks – TD Securities
FX.summary: TD Securities strategists note that FX markets remain meaningfully long the US Dollar (USD) ahead of the October FOMC, with data showing the Fed faces the strongest G10 hiking pressures.
FX.reason: Broad dollar-long positioning into a major Fed meeting is a high‑impact USD narrative (USD strength = negative for other currencies). High relevance because it describes market positioning ahead of the FOMC and cross‑G10 hiking pressures — a dominant macro driver for FX.

FX.title: Australian Dollar extends gains on RBA rate hike expectations ahead of Fed decision
FX.summary: AUD/USD extends its gains on Friday, trading around 0.7035 at the time of writing, up 0.20% on the day.
FX.reason: AUD strength vs USD on RBA rate expectations and positive flow into AUD/USD. Relevant near-term risk-on/policy divergence narrative ahead of the Fed, but not as market-wide as USD/FOMC positioning, so moderate relevance.

FX.title: Euro: Fiscal risks cap upside against US Dollar – BBH
FX.summary: Brown Brothers Harriman (BBH) strategist Elias Haddad reports EUR/USD trading defensively below 1.1200 after weaker-than-expected Eurozone PMI, which still signals robust growth.
FX.reason: Fiscal/survey weakness capping EUR upside vs USD (EUR pressure). This is a region-specific headwind to EUR flows; moderate relevance as it reinforces the broader USD‑strength / euro vulnerability theme.

FX.title: Euro slips toward 1.1200 as US economic strength overshadows Eurozone
FX.summary: EUR/USD declines for the third consecutive day on Friday, trading around 1.1200, down 0.12% at the time of writing.
FX.reason: Repeated daily losses for EUR vs USD emphasize the dominant narrative of US economic outperformance and dollar strength. Higher relevance because it reflects a sustained multi-day move across EURUSD.

FX.title: Euro: France-linked spread risks keep EUR unattractive – ING
FX.summary: Francesco Pesole at ING notes that widening French OAT-Bund and OAT-BTP spreads have yet to materially weigh on the euro, but warns that sensitivity to French sovereign risk could return rapidly if spreads approach 200bp.
FX.reason: Sovereign spread/fiscal risk is a structural EUR negative if it re-emerges; this is an important regional vulnerability that supports a cautious/negative EUR view vs USD, so moderately high relevance.

FX.title: British Pound falters near 1.3400 as US business strength lifts US Dollar
FX.summary: The Pound Sterling (GBP) retreats by about 0.16% against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday as US business activity expands, while consumer sentiment worsens, with households complaining about high prices. At the time of writing, GBP/USD trades at 1.3366.
FX.reason: GBP weakness driven by USD strength from US data — reinforces the cross-G10 dollar-strength narrative. Relevant as a G10 currency move tied to US macro, but not uniquely market-changing on its own.

FX.title: Mexican Peso: Stays under pressure as Banxico lags Fed – ING
FX.summary: Chris Turner at ING highlights that the Mexican Peso has been the weakest emerging market currency since early September, hurt by dovish Banxico rhetoric and narrowing policy spreads versus the Federal Reserve. Without a hawkish surprise at the 5 November meet
FX.reason: Banxico dovishness vs Fed is a clear EM FX policy/spread story causing MXN weakness vs USD. High relevance because it identifies the weakest EM currency and a specific central-bank event (Nov meeting) that could change flows.

FX.title: Mexican Peso recovers but faces weekly loss on Iran risk
FX.summary: The Mexican Peso (MXN) appreciates about 0.30% on Friday against the US Dollar (USD), but it remains poised to end the week with losses of more than 1% even as risk appetite soured amid a potential escalation of the Middle East conflict. The USD/MXN pair trade
FX.reason: Short-term MXN rebound against a backdrop of geopolitical risk; includes risk-premium dynamics (Iran) which can temporarily move EMFX. Modest relevance because it's a tactical recovery inside a larger downtrend.

FX.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Hammer signals rebound risk near 156.00
FX.summary: The Japanese Yen finished the week on a higher note as the USD/JPY pair registered losses of over 0.74% in the week, while holding firm daily amid a sour market mood. The pair trades at 156.85 as a ‘hammer candle pattern’ forms.
FX.reason: Technical/price-forecast piece on USD/JPY (JPY strength signalled by weekly losses and a hammer). Technical articles have capped relevance; included as a JPY-specific near-term signal rather than a macro regime shift.

FX.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Bulls challenge SMA cluster, eye 0.7100
FX.summary: The Australian Dollar finished Friday’s session with gains of over 0.22% and the week up by more than 1.20%, with the pair reclaiming the 0.7000 figure and poised to test a confluence of key resistance levels within the 0.7000-0.7100 range. At the time of writ
FX.reason: Technical bullish AUD/USD forecast reinforcing the AUD strength theme; limited relevance because it's a price-forecast/technical piece rather than new fundamental/policy news.

FX.title: Singapore Dollar: Modest upside bias against US Dollar - UOB
FX.summary: United Overseas Bank strategists (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD was little changed on Thursday, trading in a narrow band as safe-haven flows and Oil gains supported the US Dollar against Asian currencies.
FX.reason: Modest SGD upside vs USD in a narrow range; relevant for Asia/SGD flows but lower impact on the broader USD narrative. Kept for regional completeness.

FX.title: Indian Rupee: Cautious with decline risk against US Dollar – OCBC
FX.summary: OCBC strategists Christopher Wong and Sim Moh Siong say Indian Rupee's (INR) recent recovery has stalled as renewed gains in Oil prices highlight India’s external vulnerabilities.
FX.reason: Oil-driven external vulnerability implies INR downside vs USD. Regional EMFX risk story with moderate relevance given commodity sensitivity and potential capital-flow implications.

FX.title: South Korean Won: Recovery favoured on dips – OCBC
FX.summary: OCBC strategists Christopher Wong and Sim Moh Siong describe South Korean Won's (KRW) initial strength and subsequent retracement as broader risk aversion resurfaced.
FX.reason: KRW dip-buying bias in the face of renewed risk aversion — a tactical, regional FX flow dynamic. Lower relevance relative to major G10 currency regime but included as part of Asia FX flow context.

Commodities.title: Gold falls below $4,000 as Oil surge deepens weekly rout ahead of Fed
Commodities.summary: Gold (XAU/USD) price prolongs its agony, tumbling by nearly 0.60% on Friday and poised to finish the week with losses as higher energy prices increase the chances that major central banks could tighten monetary policy to control inflation.
Commodities.reason: Gold weakness driven by higher energy prices lifting rate-tightening fears (headline links energy -> tighter policy). Negative for gold (higher rates reduce bullion's appeal); clear market-flow relevance but not an exceptional structural shock.

Commodities.title: Gold eyes weekly loss of over 3% as Fed interest rate decision looms
Commodities.summary: Gold (XAU/USD) loses momentum after attempting a rebound from a three-month low of $3,986 touched during Asian trading hours. Buyers remain on the sidelines as market sentiment stays fragile.
Commodities.reason: Continued fragile sentiment and Fed-rate risk weighing on gold demand; market-level negative for bullion with moderate relevance.

Commodities.title: Silver Price Forecast: Fresh yearly low puts $50 in bears’ sight
Commodities.summary: Silver (XAG/USD) price downtrend extended on Friday, losing over 1% after hitting a new yearly low of $53.03, paving the way for sellers to challenge the $50.00 level in the foreseeable future. At the time of writing, XAG/USD trades near $54.00.
Commodities.reason: Fresh yearly lows and technical path toward $50 consistent with downside bias; silver suffering from weak safe-haven flows and industrial demand concerns — negative for silver prices with meaningful relevance.

Commodities.title: Silver Price Forecast: Bearish pressure mounts as $50 comes into focus
Commodities.summary: Silver (XAG/USD) slides to fresh yearly lows on Friday after plunging 5.8% on Thursday as concerns over AI-related investments weighed on equities, but failed to spark safe-haven demand for Silver as investors favour government bonds.
Commodities.reason: Market note linking equities/AI rotation and bond safe-haven flows to weak silver demand; negative near-term implication for silver with standard relevance.

Commodities.title: Crude Oil rises to a 22-week high on Gulf attacks
Commodities.summary: Two days of Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia and strikes on ships leaving the Strait of Hormuz have taken WTI above the $95.00-$101.00 band it held from Monday to Thursday.
Commodities.reason: Direct geopolitical supply-risk to crude (attacks in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz) has lifted the oil risk premium and driven prices to multi-week highs — strong positive for oil with high relevance.

Commodities.title: Category 2 Hurricane Isaias nears landfall, leading to production shut-ins
Commodities.summary: As of 4:00 a.m. central time on October 9, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration expects Hurricane Isaias to make landfall on the Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, creating the potential for significant disruptions to energy infrastructur
Commodities.reason: Potential Gulf production shut-ins create near-term physical supply risk for oil/NGLs; positive for energy prices with elevated relevance given regional concentration of U.S. output and infrastructure.

Commodities.title: Qatar deal to buy U.S. natural gas shows how Iran war has redrawn global energy markets
Commodities.summary: The Iran war is transforming global energy markets and benefiting U.S. companies, especially liquefied natural gas exporters.
Commodities.reason: Large LNG offtake deals and re-routing of global gas supplies amid geopolitical shocks support stronger LNG/natural gas prices and flows to U.S. exporters — positive for gas with material relevance.

Commodities.title: Saudi Arabia wants to pump 10M barrels a day. Oil may shrug it off
Commodities.reason: Potential policy-driven increase in Saudi supply is a bearish signal for crude, but the title notes markets may ignore it — include as a lower-relevance counter-signal to the prevailing geopolitical-driven oil rally.

Commodities.title: UAE closes more beaches as Gulf oil spill raises environmental concerns
Commodities.reason: Oil spill and coastal closures imply operational and logistical disruption in a regional hydrocarbon hub; modest positive for nearby crude and shipping risk premium with medium relevance.

Commodities.title: Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm
Commodities.reason: Political controversies and potential delays around a North Sea oil project (Rosebank) imply upside risk to oil via constrained supply and project postponements; moderate relevance for oil fundamentals.

Commodities.title: Energy demand set to surge as AI data centers expand across America
Commodities.reason: Structural demand tailwind for energy (power and fuels) from expanding AI data centers supports longer-term commodity demand (natural gas, diesel/electricity); positive but medium relevance to commodity prices.

Commodities.title: The Black Sea is now the world’s deadliest shipping route
Commodities.summary: Fatalities of commercial sailors caught in battle between Russia and Ukraine are outstripping deaths in the Gulf
Commodities.reason: Escalation in Black Sea shipping risk raises broader energy/shipping premiums (affecting crude and refined product flows); positive for commodity risk premia but lower direct relevance than Gulf events.

Commodities.title: Cardano holders are being asked to bet $5 million on copper hitting a new record
Commodities.reason: Market-driven speculative interest in copper (betting markets) signals bullish sentiment for industrial metals; limited direct supply/demand signal but positive for copper positioning.

Crypto.title: Bitcoin’s wealthy holders turning to loans and yield as investment habits mature: Xapo CEO
Crypto.reason: Signals maturation of the Bitcoin investor base and growth of lending/yield products that deepen liquidity and institutional-style demand. Positive for crypto adoption and market structure but not an immediate price shock.

Crypto.title: Live updates: Bitcoin holds above $81,000 as oil prices hit six-month high
Crypto.reason: Price stability above $81k supports bullish sentiment and risk appetite in crypto markets. Market-moving near-term confirmation of strength but still tied to macro/commodity moves.

Crypto.title: Bitcoin Core changes security rules as AI makes finding code bugs dangerously easy
Crypto.reason: Protocol-level security changes are a net positive for network integrity and long-term confidence, though they also highlight elevated AI-driven code-risk — modest positive relevance.

Crypto.title: Ethereum delays Glamsterdam test after security devs flag risk to existing contracts
Crypto.reason: Delay due to security risks undermines confidence in near-term Ethereum upgrades and could weigh on ETH and smart-contract activity; meaningful negative technical/regime signal for protocol momentum.

Crypto.title: Crypto under weekend pressure, bitcoin slides below $80,000 on U.S. Middle East evacuations
Crypto.reason: Geopolitical-driven risk-off caused a sharp intraweek selloff below a key $80k support level — a significant negative near-term price shock and liquidity withdrawal from crypto.

Crypto.title: HSBC rolls out its first stablecoin to over 3 million everyday app users
Crypto.reason: Major bank launching a stablecoin to millions of retail users is a high-impact institutional adoption story that materially increases on-ramps and mainstream utility for crypto — strong positive for adoption and liquidity.

Crypto.title: India's largest exchange denies hack after sleuths pointed to $16 million in suspicious outflows
Crypto.reason: Security/suspicious outflow allegations at a major exchange raise counterparty and operational risk concerns for market participants, denting trust and liquidity in the region.

Crypto.title: Senate's top Democratic investigator looking into Tether payments to Bo Hines' firm
Crypto.reason: A U.S. Senate probe into Tether payments is a major regulatory/legal risk for the largest stablecoin. This threatens market plumbing, stablecoin trust, and could have systemic negative consequences for crypto liquidity and flows.

Crypto.title: U.S. Clarity Act failure gives Asia and Middle East a competitive edge, says Apex Group CEO
Crypto.reason: Policy/regulatory failure in the U.S. implies jurisdictional fragmentation and potential relocation of crypto business to Asia/Middle East — a negative for U.S.-centric crypto growth and regulatory certainty.

Crypto.title: A16z is the latest VC giant to widen bets beyond crypto and into AI and emerging tech
Crypto.reason: Shift of major VC capital allocation away from crypto toward AI/other tech reduces available growth funding for crypto startups over the medium term — modest negative for ecosystem financing.
